cruxes.issue: Whether computers will ever be able to think like humans
cruxes.side_a: Computers will be able to think like humans or are very close to doing so
cruxes.side_b: Computers will not completely think like humans

cruxes.issue: Whether university education should be free for all courses or only for specific key professions
cruxes.side_a: University education should be free for all students/courses
cruxes.side_b: University education should only be free for specific key courses (e.g., teaching, medicine) or fees should vary by course type

cruxes.issue: Whether the disclosure requirement should be absolute or qualified

cruxes.side_b: Disclosure should be partial or qualified ('somewhat')

cruxes.issue: Whether facial recognition technology is free from bias or if it exacerbates existing prejudices against certain groups.

cruxes.side_b: Facial recognition is flawed due to inherent AI biases (e.g., against ethnic minorities) and could worsen police bias.

cruxes.issue: Whether the use of facial recognition constitutes an unacceptable invasion of privacy regarding the storage and use of personal data.
cruxes.side_a: The benefits of improved arrest rates and crime deterrence outweigh privacy concerns, or privacy is not a significant barrier to adoption.

cruxes.issue: Whether Britain's individual efforts to reduce carbon footprint are meaningful or effective

cruxes.issue: The extent to which human activity is the primary driver of climate change

cruxes.side_b: It is unknown if human influence is driving climate change, as climate changes naturally over long periods

cruxes.issue: Whether animal testing is ethically acceptable or necessary for scientific progress

cruxes.side_b: Animal testing is unethical, causes unnecessary suffering, and should be banned

cruxes.issue: Whether banning imports is a reasonable policy for national economic and social benefit

cruxes.issue: Whether taxes on the wealthiest should be increased or kept at current levels

cruxes.side_b: Taxes on the wealthiest should not be increased (or should remain neutral/not higher just for earning more)

cruxes.issue: Whether the government should fund new research into educational programs to make humans smarter
cruxes.side_a: The government should fund this research
cruxes.side_b: The government should not fund this research

cruxes.issue: Whether the UK is currently over-populated
cruxes.side_a: The UK is over-populated
cruxes.side_b: The UK is not over-populated

cruxes.issue: Whether a basic income of £10,000 is sufficient to cover basic living costs

cruxes.side_a: It would harm businesses because people would have less money to spend

cruxes.issue: Whether electric large private cars should be permitted or banned

cruxes.issue: Whether the solution to plastic bag pollution is a ban or a switch to biodegradable materials
cruxes.side_a: A ban is unnecessary; the problem is solved by switching to biodegradable plastics, which retain the benefits of plastic bags while fixing the degradation issue.
cruxes.side_b: The solution involves banning the manufacture of standard plastic bags (either immediately or conditionally) in favor of other methods like reusables or recycled plastics, rather than just switching to biodegradable versions.

cruxes.issue: Whether the retirement age should be raised, lowered, or kept the same

cruxes.side_b: CCTV should be used for serious crime only

cruxes.issue: Whether a temporary expansion of coal-fired power stations is justified as a bridge to renewable energy
cruxes.side_a: A slight expansion for a finite period (e.g., 25 years) is justified to ensure power supply and reduce costs while long-term measures are implemented

cruxes.issue: Whether a four-day workweek is feasible for all types of jobs or only specific sectors

cruxes.issue: Whether face masks should be required in specific high-risk situations like healthcare settings or for symptomatic individuals.

cruxes.issue: Whether the current electoral system is fair and democratic

cruxes.side_b: The current system is unfair, not democratic, or horrendous and needs reform

cruxes.issue: Whether the House of Lords should be retained in some form or abolished entirely
cruxes.side_a: Retain the House of Lords, potentially with adjustments or reforms
cruxes.side_b: Abolish the House of Lords

cruxes.issue: The appropriate target year for achieving carbon neutrality

cruxes.issue: Whether smoking should be banned completely or regulated/restricted

cruxes.issue: Whether the UK should pursue membership of the European Union

cruxes.side_b: The UK should not pursue membership of the EU

cruxes.issue: Whether there should be any restrictions on the number of children a person can have

cruxes.issue: Whether the UK should set a carbon neutral goal for 2050 or an earlier date

cruxes.side_b: The goal should be set for a date earlier than 2050 (e.g., 2035 or 2040)

cruxes.issue: Whether universal free childcare should be provided to all or restricted via means testing
cruxes.side_a: Universal free childcare for all
cruxes.side_b: Childcare should be means-tested or subsidized rather than universally free

cruxes.issue: Whether the price of prescription drugs should be capped

cruxes.issue: Whether a dog is definitively a better companion than a cat

cruxes.issue: The nature of the animal's independence and attachment to humans

cruxes.side_b: Independence is a neutral trait or a pro, and cats are capable of being wonderful companions in their own way

cruxes.issue: Whether the provision of free life-saving treatment should be restricted to domestic residents or extended to any child regardless of nationality or residency.
cruxes.side_a: Treatment should be provided to any child who needs it, regardless of origin or residency status.
cruxes.side_b: Treatment should be restricted to the country's own children/citizens and not provided to children from other countries.

cruxes.issue: Whether 16-year-olds possess sufficient maturity and life experience to make informed political decisions

cruxes.side_b: 16-year-olds are knowledgeable, mature enough, and their inclusion balances the electorate

cruxes.issue: Whether the NHS is fundamentally a socialist institution

cruxes.issue: Whether the ban should be implemented gradually or immediately
cruxes.side_a: The ban should be introduced gradually to allow for economic adjustment and finding alternatives

cruxes.issue: Whether a Universal Basic Income would reduce work incentives and lead to labor shortages

cruxes.side_b: UBI would lead to people doing nothing and lower-paid jobs not being filled

cruxes.issue: Whether the UK should adopt a Universal Basic Income
cruxes.side_a: The UK should adopt or trial a Universal Basic Income
cruxes.side_b: The UK should not adopt a Universal Basic Income

cruxes.issue: Whether supermarkets should be permitted to sell meat from non-human animals
cruxes.side_a: It is okay/acceptable for supermarkets to sell meat from non-human animals
cruxes.side_b: Supermarkets should not be allowed to sell meat from non-human animals

cruxes.issue: Whether the basic income should be universal or conditional on work/skill
cruxes.side_a: The income should be universal and unconditional, allowing people to choose whether to work.
cruxes.side_b: The income should be conditional, dependent on skill level, or not provided to those who do not want to work.

cruxes.issue: Whether the government should prioritize job creation over direct income provision
cruxes.side_a: The government should create jobs to sustain life and boost the economy.
cruxes.side_b: The government should provide a basic income to all citizens.

cruxes.issue: Whether the leaving age should be reduced to 16 or kept at 18
cruxes.side_a: The leaving age should be reduced to 16
cruxes.side_b: The leaving age should not be reduced to 16 (should remain 18)

cruxes.issue: Whether eating meat is morally permissible or inherently wrong
cruxes.side_a: It is not okay to eat meat because it is inhumane and unnecessary
cruxes.side_b: It is okay to eat meat because it is natural for humans

cruxes.issue: Whether the current extent of meat consumption is excessive and should be reduced
cruxes.side_a: The extent of meat consumption is very high and people should move away from it
cruxes.side_b: It is a matter of personal choice and not a problem if others consume it

cruxes.issue: Whether the existence of royal privileges is fundamentally wrong or acceptable if wealth is redistributed
cruxes.side_a: It is wrong to give special privileges based on family status; they should earn their own money and not rely on the state.
cruxes.side_b: It is not necessarily wrong if they prioritize the community and donate most of their wealth; opposing their existence entirely is counterproductive to human nature.

cruxes.issue: Whether the government is currently taking significant action to protect privacy
cruxes.side_a: The government is doing a lot to protect individual privacy
cruxes.side_b: The government is not doing enough, or its actions are ineffective/untrustworthy

cruxes.issue: Whether the proposal should be allowed or rejected

cruxes.side_b: The proposal should be rejected

cruxes.issue: Whether the system is prone to abuse, bullying, or misuse
cruxes.side_a: The system is prone to abuse, bullying, or misuse
cruxes.side_b: The system is not prone to abuse or has no downside if voluntary

cruxes.issue: Whether the government should provide universal free childcare
cruxes.side_a: The government should provide universal free childcare
cruxes.side_b: The government should not provide universal free childcare

cruxes.issue: Whether childcare is the responsibility of parents or the state/taxpayers
cruxes.side_a: Childcare is the responsibility of parents
cruxes.side_b: The state has a duty to care for children (alongside parents)

cruxes.issue: Whether nuclear power should be stopped immediately or retained for the time being
cruxes.side_a: Nuclear power should be stopped (or we should work towards stopping it, even if not immediately)
cruxes.side_b: Nuclear power should not be stopped and should be kept for the time being

cruxes.issue: Whether the reliability of nuclear power is a sufficient reason to retain it over alternatives
cruxes.side_a: Nuclear power is reliable and necessary for modern society, making it superior to current alternatives
cruxes.side_b: The reliability of nuclear power is not a sufficient reason to retain it, or the focus should be on the damaging effects and better use of funds

cruxes.issue: Whether capitalism primarily improves lives for the majority or significantly harms the bottom tier
cruxes.side_a: Capitalism improves lives by providing opportunities, wealth, and comfort for people generally
cruxes.side_b: Capitalism makes those at the bottom much worse off due to low wages and lack of support

cruxes.issue: Whether capitalism allows for upward mobility or keeps people at a flat level of mediocrity
cruxes.side_a: Capitalism allows people to rise to the top and make something exceptional of their lives
cruxes.side_b: Capitalism keeps people at a flat level of mediocrity (implied by the preference for the chance to be rich or poor over mediocrity, contrasting with the 'flat level' description)

cruxes.issue: Whether the number of immigrants should be increased
cruxes.side_a: Yes, the number should be increased
cruxes.side_b: No, the number should not be increased due to resource constraints

cruxes.issue: Whether a longer fixed term prevents or enables the abuse of power and corruption.
cruxes.side_a: A longer term is beneficial because it prevents politicians from abusing power.
cruxes.side_b: A longer term is detrimental because it allows politicians to lock themselves into power, leading to corruption and incompetence.

cruxes.issue: Whether stricter regulations are necessary or if current standards are sufficient
cruxes.side_a: Stricter regulations are needed to ensure safety, prevent obesity, and ensure accountability
cruxes.side_b: Current regulations are sufficient and stricter rules would cause unnecessary costs or negative impacts

cruxes.issue: Whether banning chemicals is an effective deterrent against bomb-making
cruxes.side_a: A ban is ineffective because determined individuals will find other sources or methods
cruxes.side_b: A ban is a necessary and effective measure to prevent the rampant usage of bombs

cruxes.issue: Whether access to bombs serves as a deterrent to war
cruxes.side_a: Access to bombs acts as a deterrent to war
cruxes.side_b: Bombs are harmful and their usage should be prevented, implying they do not serve a positive deterrent role

cruxes.issue: Whether full two-way conversation with animals is possible
cruxes.side_a: Full communication and two-way conversation will be achieved
cruxes.side_b: Full two-way conversation is unlikely due to cognitive and linguistic differences

cruxes.issue: Whether children under 13 should be allowed to use social media at all

cruxes.issue: Whether the emphasis on teaching should be placed on the nation's own history or on the histories of other nations
cruxes.side_a: More emphasis should be placed on the history and values of the nation
cruxes.side_b: More emphasis should be placed on the history and values of other nations

cruxes.issue: Whether the government should provide subsidies for children's breakfasts
cruxes.side_a: The government should not provide subsidies; it is not their responsibility and should be left to parents or the community sector.
cruxes.side_b: The government should provide subsidies to ensure children have nutritious breakfasts.

cruxes.issue: Whether the UK government should prioritize domestic issues (like NHS and housing) over space exploration funding
cruxes.side_a: Space exploration should be funded as it furthers scientific progress and has ancillary benefits, outweighing or justifying the cost despite other needs
cruxes.side_b: Domestic issues such as the NHS, housing, and climate change are more pressing and should be prioritized over space exploration

cruxes.issue: Whether taxes are currently too high for the respondent
cruxes.side_a: Taxes are not too high for me (or are broadly correct/reasonable)
cruxes.side_b: Taxes are too high for me

cruxes.issue: Whether higher earners should pay significantly higher taxes to subsidize others
cruxes.side_a: Higher earners should pay high percentages to subsidize less well-off people
cruxes.side_b: People should keep the majority of their income and governments are inefficient/wasteful

cruxes.issue: Whether free school meals should be provided to all children or only to those who meet specific financial criteria
cruxes.side_a: All schoolchildren should receive a free daily hot meal regardless of income
cruxes.side_b: Free school meals should be means-tested or based on need, not provided to everyone

cruxes.issue: Whether the United Kingdom should be a member of the European Union
cruxes.side_a: The United Kingdom should be a member of the European Union
cruxes.side_b: The United Kingdom should not be a member of the European Union

cruxes.issue: Whether the government should implement an opt-out system for organ donation
cruxes.side_a: The government should create an opt-out system
cruxes.side_b: The government should not create an opt-out system (should be opt-in or individual choice)

cruxes.side_a: The age of 18 is too strict; individuals aged 16 and upwards are adult enough to make their own decisions and should not be subject to the same restrictions as younger children.

cruxes.issue: Whether universities should be treated as businesses or supported by the government
cruxes.side_a: Universities are like a business and need to cover costs
cruxes.side_b: Universities are not a business and should be supported by the government

cruxes.issue: Whether society should actively discourage or restrict parents from having children after age 50

cruxes.side_b: UBI leads to a more divided society due to resentment between taxpayers and recipients

cruxes.issue: The impact of UBI on work incentives and motivation
cruxes.side_a: UBI provides stability and quality of life without negative social consequences
cruxes.side_b: UBI removes the incentive to work, making people lazy and demotivated

cruxes.side_b: No, the government should not subsidize electric vehicles as the money is better spent on other things like public transport and individuals should pay for their own choices

cruxes.side_a: Yes, identical products should be legally required to have the same price
cruxes.side_b: No, supermarkets should not be legally obliged to charge the same price

cruxes.issue: Whether price uniformity should apply to all products or only specific categories

cruxes.side_b: Price uniformity should not apply to all products (e.g., exclude own-brand or allow competition for non-branded items)

cruxes.side_b: Repossession is not appropriate; banks should help restructure or extend the mortgage to avoid homelessness

cruxes.issue: Whether individual actions are sufficient or meaningful compared to the impact of large corporations.
cruxes.side_a: Individual actions, even if small, make an impact when everyone does their bit.

cruxes.side_a: Taxation is primarily a way for the government to make more money, which is an annoyance rather than a deterrent.

cruxes.issue: Whether the government is failing to tackle child obesity

cruxes.side_a: The government should take active measures (e.g., vouchers, regulation, school mandates) to address the issue
cruxes.side_b: It is the parents' responsibility, and government intervention (like taxes) is excessive or counterproductive

cruxes.issue: Whether the moral obligation to support international development is primarily driven by historical guilt (slavery/colonization) or by general ethical duties of wealth and global interdependence.
cruxes.side_a: The obligation stems specifically from historical wrongs such as slavery and colonization, requiring the UK to 'right the wrongs'.
cruxes.side_b: The obligation stems from general moral duties of developed/wealthy nations to help the less developed, or from mutual benefits like trade and global stability, without necessarily centering on historical reparations.

cruxes.issue: Whether the priority of funds should be directed to international development or to addressing domestic issues within the UK.
cruxes.side_a: International development should be supported, and the focus should not be diverted to domestic issues; in fact, domestic problems are partly blamed on government policies that ignore international context or blame immigrants.
cruxes.side_b: There is a significant obligation to consider the value of money being directed to other countries *rather than* fixing many issues that have arisen in this country (crime, poverty, etc.), implying a tension or trade-off where domestic needs might take precedence or require careful balancing.

cruxes.issue: Whether the nations should become independent countries
cruxes.side_a: They should become independent countries
cruxes.side_b: They should not become independent countries

cruxes.issue: Whether the economic impact of independence would be negative for ordinary people
cruxes.side_a: Independence would cause economic hardship and make life more difficult for the average person
cruxes.side_b: Independence might make countries better off financially or allow for fairer resource distribution

cruxes.side_a: Encouraging national pride leads to dangerous nationalism, racism, and negative attitudes towards other cultures

cruxes.side_a: There is nothing to be proud of due to a history of slavery, empire, and mistreatment, and the current state is poor
cruxes.side_b: National pride is important to remember history, whether good or bad, and can galvanize the population

cruxes.issue: Whether private property and the ability to accumulate intergenerational wealth should be abolished or restricted.
cruxes.side_a: Private property should be abolished or inherited wealth should be abolished to prevent inequality.
cruxes.side_b: Private property should not be abolished as it is essential for incentives and economic stability.

cruxes.issue: Whether there should be a limit on the amount of wealth that can be passed down between generations.
cruxes.side_a: There should be a limit on intergenerational wealth accumulation to address the rich-poor divide.
cruxes.side_b: There should be no limit; homeowners should be free to pass on any accumulated wealth.

cruxes.issue: Whether the UK should ban imports from countries with low minimum wages
cruxes.side_a: The UK should ban such imports to address exploitation and poverty wages
cruxes.side_b: The UK should not ban such imports due to economic necessity, global market realities, or relative cost of living

cruxes.issue: Whether the NHS should lower antibiotic prices regardless of the financial impact on the system
cruxes.side_a: The NHS should lower prices to ensure accessibility, even if it requires increasing taxes or accepting higher costs
cruxes.side_b: The NHS should not lower prices for expensive antibiotics to protect the system from increasing spending

cruxes.issue: Whether a basic income should be provided to everyone or only to those who meet specific criteria (such as willingness to work or financial need).
cruxes.side_a: The government should provide a basic income to everyone.
cruxes.side_b: The government should not provide a basic income to everyone, but only to those who are able/willing to work or who have specific financial needs.

cruxes.issue: Whether animal products are necessary for human health or if alternatives are sufficient
cruxes.side_a: Animal products are necessary for health and alternatives do not have the same effect
cruxes.side_b: Alternatives exist and are sufficient, or animal products are not strictly necessary

cruxes.issue: Whether the decision to remove animal products should be a personal choice or a collective goal
cruxes.side_a: It should be a personal choice and individuals should not be judged
cruxes.side_b: We should try to remove them (implying a collective or normative push)

cruxes.issue: Whether private-sector involvement in the health system should be permitted at all
cruxes.side_a: Some parts of the health system may be suited to the private sector, provided the NHS remains available to all
cruxes.side_b: Private-sector organisations should not run any parts of the health system, as profit motives are incompatible with healthcare access and equity

cruxes.issue: Whether the primary justification for allowing investment is the necessity of foreign capital for infrastructure funding.
cruxes.side_a: Allowing investment is justified because foreign money is already prevalent in infrastructure and the public benefits from it, making the 'cat out of the bag'.
cruxes.side_b: Allowing investment is not justified by financial necessity or existing foreign capital; instead, it should be rejected or heavily restricted due to security, human rights, and geopolitical risks.

cruxes.issue: Whether there is a fundamental moral difference between eating dogs and eating other animals
cruxes.side_a: There is no fundamental moral difference between the lives of different animals, so consuming dogs is not morally objectionable in principle
cruxes.side_b: There is a moral difference; eating dogs is morally wrong or cruel, often due to their status as companions or their capacity for emotion

cruxes.issue: Whether sugar provides necessary nutritional benefits or energy for growth
cruxes.side_a: Sugar is required for a healthy diet and provides necessary energy for exercise and growth
cruxes.side_b: Sugar provides no benefit and is purely harmful, with no nutritional necessity

cruxes.issue: Whether sugar should be a regular part of the diet or a rare exception
cruxes.side_a: Sugar should be allowed within moderation as part of a balanced diet or for regular treats
cruxes.side_b: Sugar should not be part of the diet at all and should only be an exception (or avoided entirely after age 2)

cruxes.issue: Whether the primary focus of government action should be on restricting gun ownership itself or on controlling the individuals who own guns.
cruxes.side_a: The government should take action to reduce the prevalence of guns and gun ownership (restricting the objects).
cruxes.side_b: Gun ownership itself is not the issue; the focus should be on controls for the people who own the guns.

cruxes.issue: Whether the NHS is a model that other countries should aspire to
cruxes.side_a: Yes, the NHS is a model to aspire to because it provides free healthcare to all citizens
cruxes.side_b: No, the NHS is not a model to aspire to due to issues like disease management focus, long waiting times, and lack of preventative care

cruxes.issue: Whether making divorce easier would lead to people abandoning relationships too quickly instead of trying to work on them.
cruxes.side_a: Making divorce easier is beneficial and does not carry the risk of people giving up on relationships too soon.
cruxes.side_b: Making divorce easier would cause people to seek divorce instead of trying to work on their relationships first.

cruxes.issue: Whether parents should have the right to withdraw their children from sex education
cruxes.side_a: Parents should be able to withdraw their children
cruxes.side_b: Parents should not be able to withdraw their children

cruxes.issue: Whether lying to a parliamentary select committee should be made illegal
